title: UK GDP quarterly national accounts, Apr-Jun 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the Blue Book 2026 revisions land here, 41 days after their own impact article made them public
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/gdpquarterlynationalaccountsukapriltojune2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — reads verbatim 'GDP quarterly national accounts, UK: April to June 2026', '30 September 2026 at 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', and carries the accredited-official-statistics kitemark. Second publisher primary the same session: the live 'GDP first quarterly estimate, UK: April to June 2026' bulletin (published 2026-08-13) names its own 'Next release: 30 September 2026'. Cadence scraped direct from four pages of the publisher's own past-release listing (ons.gov.uk/economy/grossdomesticproductgdp/bulletins/quarterlynationalaccounts/previousreleases, HTTP 200 each): 40 consecutive editions 2016-09-30 to 2026-06-30, and every one of the 10 September editions falls on the LAST WORKING DAY of September — 30 Sept when it is a weekday (2016, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025), the Friday before when it is not (2017-09-29, 2018-09-28, 2023-09-29). 2026-09-30 is a Wednesday. Filed estimate on the same two counts as every ONS entry on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: Canonical file written 2026-09-09 by the never-assessed initial research of this id, which existed only as proposals/uk-quarterly-national-accounts-2026-09-30.from-uk-public-sector-finances-2026-09-22.json (read in full first; it stays where it is and is now shadowed). The proposing lane framed this as the cleanest test of when the 2026-10-28 Budget's OBR forecast closes, because the OBR excluded the analogous 2024-09-30 quarterly national accounts from its October 2024 pre-measures forecast. That framing is upheld but narrowed on two counts the research found. FIRST, the content is already public: the Blue Book 2026 impact articles were published 2026-08-20 (ons.gov.uk .../bluebook2026impactongdpandmaincomponents/2026-08-20, fetched direct) with the 1997-2024 revisions in full — 2024 nominal GDP +0.5% to GBP 2,905bn, 2024 real growth +0.1pp to 1.1% — and state that 'The next quarterly national accounts release on 30 September 2026 will incorporate these improvements into our official estimates'. What 09-30 adds is the carry-through into 2025 and H1 2026, not the revisions themselves, so an OBR forecast closing 2026-09-22/24 can already see the annual picture. SECOND, the 2024 precedent has a third outcome the proposal's binary missed: Box 2.2 of the October 2024 EFO ('Blue Book 2024 revisions') examined the excluded release anyway and judged the revisions gave limited new information on current economic conditions, leaving the forecast broadly unchanged (READ DIRECT 2026-09-16 by this event's own pulse check, superseding the initial research's search relay: obr.uk/box/blue-book-2024-revisions/ returned HTTP 200 where it had 403'd five lanes, and obr.uk/efo/economic-and-fiscal-outlook-october-2024/ states verbatim that the Blue Book 2024 data 'released on 30 September ... were published too close to the Budget date for us to be able to include them in our pre-measures forecast that was finalised on 26 September'; probe-ref.blocked is now empty. The autumn-2026 forecast timetable is still unobtained and cannot be obtained early: obr.uk/autumn-2026-forecast-date-announced/ (HTTP 200, updated 2026-09-10) says the agreed timetable will be set out 'in the foreword of the EFO when it is published on 28 October alongside the Budget'). Tiered LOW and symbols [] on a MEASURED basis, not an inherited one: across 40 QNA release days since 2016-09-30, no series this book can reach shows an elevated move — IGLT.L 0.74x an ordinary day (t = -2.09), FTSE 0.77x (t = -2.03), ^TNX 0.73x (t = -2.40), SPY 1.04x (t = 0.30) — and every statistically significant result points QUIETER. The operational point for 2026-09-30 is the opposite of the sibling 09-22 print's: this calendar tracks 18 events on that date (recounted 2026-09-16; 56 within five days -- the initial research's '27' came from a counting method that session's own probe-ref, listing 13 on-date siblings, does not reproduce), including PCE (high, confirmed), the FY2027 federal funding deadline (high), the BEA's own Q2 2026 third estimate, ADP, Chicago PMI and quarter-end index rebalances, so no move that day is attributable to a 07:00 London GDP revision. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this. Date re-verified direct 2026-09-16 (HTTP 200): the ONS release page still reads '30 September 2026 7:00am' and 'This release is not yet published', with no change notice.
